title: Design the defaults-learning loop in docs/design/defaults-loop.md
summary: Docs-only job: write docs/design/defaults-loop.md describing how Jev matches interventions and corrections to defaults and how repeats become proposed, versioned defaults for review. No code, no defaults.toml edits; proposals are review-only.

defaults_applied.how: Design written down first with alternatives, before any build.
Claims cite records; numbers measured or labeled estimates.
No secrets or personal data in the doc.

assumptions: Records are not visible to me; the producer must find the cited repeats in what it can read, and label any it cannot verify.
Design doc follows the style of existing docs/design/*.md, including alternatives.
Review of the design happens in a later job.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/design/defaults-loop.md exists and is grounded in real intervention/correction records, citing them, including the four repeats: CHANGELOG excluded by scope criteria (x4), reader token budget blocking (x4), design/review/build bundled into one job, config field and its use in one commit.

It states what Jev decides (matching a record to a default id with a probability, clustering/paraphrase, drafting statement text) versus what deterministic code decides (threshold, id uniqueness, version bump, validation via DefaultsModel::parse, writing the proposal).
It specifies the proposal format: fields id, statement, applies_to, version bump, and sources citing records, with an example.
It describes how a proposal reaches the user for review, and that Athena never edits defaults.toml itself; proposals are review-only.
It describes Jev calibration before trust: shadow mode, labeled set from past records, scoring rule, and promotion criteria; and addresses the D31 exclusion of Jev.
It lists alternatives considered, and numbers cited are measured from records or labeled as estimates. No secrets or personal data appear.
No Rust, defaults.toml, or governance files change.

out_of_scope: Editing defaults.toml or bumping its version
departures: Docs-only single file, slightly cheaper than reference; verification risk from unverifiable record citations.
